<STRUCT_0001>
The following lemma is a bit different to the analogue for algebraic
spaces. To compare take a look at
Morphisms of Spaces,
Lemma <REF_0001>.

<MATH_0002> be morphisms of algebraic stacks.

<STRUCT_0003> If <MATH_0005> is quasi-DM then so is <MATH_0006>.

<MATH_0009> is separated.
<STRUCT_0005> If <MATH_0010> is quasi-separated and
<MATH_0011> is quasi-separated, then <MATH_0012> is quasi-separated.
<STRUCT_0006>

Proof of (4). Assume <MATH_0017> is quasi-separated and <MATH_0018> is
quasi-separated. Consider the factorization
<MATH_0019>
of the diagonal morphism of <MATH_0020>. Both morphisms are
representable by algebraic spaces and the second one is quasi-separated, see
Lemmas <REF_0007> and
<REF_0008>.
Hence for any scheme <MATH_0021> and morphism
<MATH_0022>

<MATH_0023>
such that <MATH_0024> is quasi-separated.
The composition <MATH_0025> is quasi-compact and quasi-separated

Hence <MATH_0027> is quasi-separated by
Morphisms of Spaces,
Lemma <REF_0009>.
And <MATH_0028> is quasi-compact by

Thus <MATH_0029> is quasi-separated.

Hence for any scheme <MATH_0034> and morphism

<MATH_0036>

The composition <MATH_0038> is proper as we have assumed that
<MATH_0039> is quasi-separated. Hence <MATH_0040> is proper by
Morphisms of Spaces,
Lemma <REF_0013>
which means that <MATH_0041> is separated.
